name: agedu
desc: Unix utility for tracking down wasted disk space
why: Maps wasted disk space via a web-browsable index, a classic Tatham tool with a satisfying hidden structure.

brief.what_it_is: agedu is a Unix command-line utility for finding out where disk space is being wasted. Per the brew description it tracks down wasted disk space and presents results as a web-browsable index. I could not read the project's homepage or README, so this is based only on the Homebrew formula description and the scout notes; the executable is named agedu.
brief.why_it_exists: The scout notes describe it as a classic Tatham tool, which suggests the author is Simon Tatham, but I could not confirm the author's own framing of the problem from the README.
brief.install_notes: Installed via Homebrew (brew install agedu); the formula installs an executable called agedu. No further installation steps, runtimes, or configuration were visible to me because the pages did not load.
brief.standout: The scout notes call out a web-browsable index of disk usage and a 'satisfying hidden structure' that I could not verify from the source material I could read.
